chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rib'i who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have a palm grove in Basra, so I sell it, and I name the price, and I exclude the kurra (a unit of measurement) of dates, or more, or a cluster of dates.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the sale for two years?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, that is a great matter among us.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'As for you, if you are saying that, then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had permitted that, but they were unjust to each other, so he (peace be upon him) said, 'The fruit is not sold until its goodness appears.'

key_terms.الْكُرَّ: A specific unit of measurement for dates

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling palm fruits by specifying a price and excluding a portion, or selling for multiple years?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the permissibility of selling palm groves by specifying a price while excluding a fixed quantity (such as a *kurra* or cluster) or selling the yield for two years, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s initial allowance. However, to prevent disputes (*tazalamu*) arising from uncertainty (*gharar*) in quality, the Imam establishes the critical condition that the fruit must visibly show signs of ripeness and suitability before the transaction is finalized. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing commercial flexibility with the prevention of hidden defects in trade.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rabie who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There is a palm tree for me at Al-Basra. So I sell it, and I name (determine) the fruits, and exclude Al-Kurra (a unit of measurement) from the fruits, or more, or a cluster of the dates’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Can I sell it (yield) for the two years?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! That is a great matter among us’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But you, if you are saying that, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had Permitted that, but they were unjust to each other, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘You must not buy it until fruits appear and are out of danger (of dying)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rib’iy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I have palm tree fruits in Basrah. I sell them for a certain price excluding one Kur (a certain measurement) of the dates or more or the cluster of dates.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘There is no offense in it.’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, what do you say about selling for two years?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘There is no offense in it.’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, this is great among us.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘As you mentioned it, the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, had made it permissible but they wronged each other. He, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘You must not buy it until fruits appear and are out of danger.”’
